sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 3.3% a year from $65.1 billion in FY2017 to $87.0 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F201].
The window is not a smooth line: FY2019 operating margin collapsed to 8.1% from 20.0% [F22][F23], then recovered to 22.1% in FY2020 [F24].

The FY2019 trough came from an $8.3 billion asset impairment charge, including $6.8 billion of Shave Care goodwill, driven by currency devaluations, decelerating category growth and tougher competition [X109][X112][P62].
FY2020's rebound reflected the base-period charge plus higher sales and gross margin, with volume lifted by pandemic demand for cleaning and health products [P71][P72].
The US was the growth engine for most of the window, contributing +4.0pp of FY2020 revenue growth and +2.2pp in FY2024 [D518][D530].
In FY2026 the pattern flipped: Non-US contributed +3.1pp of the 3.3% growth while the US added just +0.1pp [D511][D536][D457].
FY2026 net sales rose 3% on favorable foreign exchange of 2% and pricing of 1%, with unit volume and mix unchanged [P26].
Operating costs grew 2.1pp faster than revenue in FY2026, at 5.3% cost of revenue growth against 3.3% revenue growth [D482][D472][D457].
Diluted EPS grew 1.7% in FY2026 against net income growth of 0.5%, helped by a 1.3% lower diluted share count [D461][D459][D476].
FY2026 operating margin of 22.7% sat above the 22.1% window median but below the 24.3% FY2025 high [F30][D648][D647].
The 1.6pp operating margin decline came from a lower gross margin and higher marketing spending, with cost of revenue costing 1.0pp and SG&A 0.6pp [D470][D483][D485][P25].
In FY2026 net margin of 18.4% sat 4.3pp below the 22.7% operating margin, a gap narrowed by $1.1 billion of other non-operating income [F50][F30][X108].
That other income rose $922 million mainly on the prior-year Argentina translation charge and the Glad joint venture dissolution gain [P24].
FY2026 operating cash flow of $19.6 billion was 1.22x net income, and free cash flow of $15.1 billion was 0.94x [F80][D444][F100][D445].
Free cash flow margin of 17.4% was in line with the 17.2% window median [D441][D654].
Operating cash flow rose 10% as net earnings plus non-cash items generated about $19.5 billion, while inventory consumed $641 million on safety stock and new products [P3].
Capex of $4.4 billion was 5.1% of revenue and 1.40x D&A, the highest capex-to-D&A ratio in the window [F90][D440][D446].
Net cash was -$24.2 billion, or -27.8% of revenue, against a staples peer median of -1.0% and a 33rd percentile rank among six peers [D450][D451][D677][D676].
The current ratio of 0.68x sits below the 0.72x window median, with working capital of -$12.5 billion [F180][D663][F170].
Buybacks of $5.0 billion plus dividends of $10.2 billion were 100.7% of free cash flow in FY2026 [X134][X144][D453].
Long-term debt fell 8.6% to $22.8 billion while equity grew 3.9% to $54.3 billion [F190][D468][F200][D467].
The current ratio has been below 1.0x every year of the window and stood at 0.68x in FY2026 [F180][F171].
This is structural for a negative-working-capital consumer staples model rather than a liquidity warning, given $9.9 billion of cash [F140].
Buybacks and dividends exceeded free cash flow in FY2025 at 116.6% and FY2026 at 100.7% [D402][D453].
Payout above free cash flow leaves little room if capex keeps rising, and the gap is bridged with debt [D446].
Whether FY2027 operating margin holds above the 22.1% window median or slips toward the 8.1% low, reported in the FY2027 10-K [D648][D646].
Whether capex as a share of revenue stays above the 5.1% FY2026 level or falls back toward the 3.7% FY2023 level [D440][D285].
Whether buybacks plus dividends fall back below the 100.7% of free cash flow recorded in FY2026, reported in the FY2027 10-K [D453].
